outcome: Part (1), whether the Borel monadic theory of the real order is decidable, has been claimed answered affirmatively in two unrefereed arXiv preprints by different authors (Manthe, first posted 1 Oct 2024; Dzamonja, first posted 28 Dec 2025), with no journal acceptance or published verification found in any source I could open; part (2), whether the monadic theory of well-ordering is consistently decidable, has no event in the window that bears on it, and the sources still describe it as open.
problem_asks: Two questions, asked as separate yes/no questions in one bullet. (1) BMTO: is the monadic second-order theory of the real order (R, <=) decidable when the set quantifier ranges over Borel subsets of R (not over all subsets of R, and not only over F_sigma or closed sets)? (2) MTWO: is the monadic (second-order) theory of well-ordering consistently decidable, i.e. is there a consistent scenario, relative to ZFC, in which the monadic theory of the well-orders is decidable? The bullet names no set-theoretic hypothesis; Shelah's Conjecture 0.3 (V=L plus no weakly compact cardinal) is one such scenario, and that reading is recorded here as the working reading.

events.what_happened: Sven Manthe, 'The Borel monadic theory of order is decidable', arXiv:2410.00887 (single author, math.LO). Claims that the monadic theory of (R, <=) with set quantification restricted to Borel sets is decidable, and says this answers Shelah's open question (the paper cites it as Shelah 1975 Conjecture 7B, and also as the open question in Gurevich's 1985 survey, p. 503). The abstract adds that the theory stays decidable with quantification over sigma-combinations of analytic sets, that the Boolean combinations of F_sigma sets form an elementary substructure of the Borel sets, and that under determinacy hypotheses the proof extends to larger classes of sets. Per the HTML text as summarised by my fetch, Corollaries 1.4 and 1.5 are conditional on projective determinacy and on ZF+DC+Determinacy respectively. Talks listed (listings not opened): Oxford, Nov 2024; Seminaire General de Logique, Paris, 15 Dec 2025.
events.revisions: v1 1 Oct 2024 (38 KB); v2 9 Mar 2026 (54 KB). The abstract page and the PDF metadata do not say what changed in v2; I did not identify the change. No journal reference on the abstract page; Manthe's own listings (search summary, not opened) show it as an arXiv preprint only.
events.delivers: Answers part (1) affirmatively for the real order: the MSO theory of (R, <=) with set quantifiers over Borel subsets of R is decidable (Theorem 1.1, as quoted from the HTML). Also decidable with quantification over sigma-combinations of analytic sets (abstract). Per a search summary, the decision procedure needs iterated exponential time. Does not address quantification over all subsets of R (undecidable under CH, Shelah 1975), the 2^(<=omega) tree, or well-orders.
events.remains: Part (2), MTWO, entirely. Also the 2^(<=omega) tree version (lexicographic order with prefix relation), which the paper itself says remains open and whose methods it says seem insufficient for.

checked_by.what_they_did: Thanked in the acknowledgements for suggestions, proofreading and discussions. The paper does not say that he checked the proof, and no separate public statement from him was found.

events.time_since_posted: 24 months from v1 (1 Oct 2024 to 12 Oct 2026); about 7 months since v2. No independent public engagement found beyond the acknowledgements and the 2026 LICS paper, which Manthe co-authored.
events.direction: Answers part (1) affirmatively, i.e. decidable. Cuts toward decidability, the direction Shelah conjectured for the reals (7B in the paper's own numbering). Not a counterexample.

events.what_happened: Mirna Dzamonja, 'MSO logic of the real order with the set quantifiers ranging over the Borel sets', arXiv:2512.23003 (single author, math.LO). Claims (a) the MSO theory of the real order with set quantifiers over Borel sets is decidable (the strong form, one quantifier domain for all Borel sets), with the paper saying 'We confirm this conjecture'; and (b) the weak form, with a separate quantifier for each Borel level, is decidable and interpretable in S2S. Method: well-levelled orders, used to code Borel sets of arbitrary complexity into branch sets of trees (Definition 2.12, Lemma 2.14); the strong form uses Buchi's decidability of MSO(omega_1, <). The paper cites the conjecture as Shelah [21, Conjecture 7A], which conflicts with Shelah's own numbering (see disputes). Acknowledgements thank HUJI seminars and name Joan Bagaria as having suggested in conversation that the idea could be used in descriptive set theory. A 2025 'announcement' by Dzamonja, mentioned in the 2026 LICS paper, is not found as a primary source; under the first-written-argument rule it is dated to this write-up.
events.revisions: v1 28 Dec 2025 (33 KB); v2 5 Jan 2026; v3 6 Jan 2026; v4 13 Jan 2026; v5 20 Jan 2026 (40 KB). Comments on the abstract page: Definition 2.12 was changed 'to fit how it was actually used in the rest of the paper', which allows a more direct proof of Lemma 2.14, and some typos were fixed. A search summary of the arXiv comments says the v4 text is the version submitted for publication; I did not confirm that on the page. No journal reference listed.
events.delivers: Answers part (1) affirmatively for the real order: decidability of the MSO theory of (R, <) with set quantifiers over Borel sets (strong form), and decidability of the level-by-level weak form (also interpretable in S2S). Restricted to the real order; the paper does not address the 2^(<=omega) tree. Says nothing about well-orders beyond using Buchi's decidability of MSO(omega_1, <) as an ingredient.
events.remains: Part (2), MTWO, entirely. The 2^(<=omega) tree version is not covered by the abstract, so it remains open as far as this paper is concerned.
events.time_since_posted: About 9.5 months from v1 (28 Dec 2025 to 12 Oct 2026); about 9 months since v5. No referee report or journal acceptance found. See doubts for the one public statement that concerns correctness.
events.doubts: No journal acceptance or referee report was found in the sources. The 2026 LICS paper by Bojanczyk, Casares, Manthe and Parys is reported, in a search-result summary of its text, to state that a proof of both conjectures was announced by Dzamonja in 2025 and that 'we could not confirm its correctness'. I could not open that paper's text, so the exact wording, and whether it refers to this arXiv preprint or to an earlier announcement, is unverified. The author's own comments record a change to Definition 2.12 after v1; I did not compare the versions to see what the proof relied on before that change.
events.direction: Answers part (1) affirmatively, for both the strong form (the one the bullet asks about) and the weak form. Cuts toward decidability. Not a counterexample.

events.what_happened: Mikolaj Bojanczyk, Antonio Casares, Sven Manthe, Pawel Parys, 'Automata for MSO over Infinite Trees with Quantification over Borel Sets of Branches', LICS 2026 (LIPIcs vol. 380, pp. 21:1-21:24; DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.LICS.2026.21). Concerns the tree 2^(<=omega) with set quantifiers restricted to Borel sets, which is a different structure from the real order. The abstract says it introduces a suitable automaton model and shows that most of the automata-theoretic proof of Rabin's tree theorem extends to it; the one missing piece is a conjecture about finite-memory determinacy in certain games, which the paper states, proves in restricted cases, and gives memory lower bounds for. The full text was not readable; the claims about Dzamonja and Manthe in the paper come from a search-result summary only.
events.delivers: Partial progress on the 2^(<=omega) Borel question, conditional on a finite-memory determinacy conjecture: the automaton approach works except for that conjecture, and the conjecture is proved in restricted cases. Does not decide the 2^(<=omega) question. Does not address the real order or well-orders.
events.remains: Decidability of MSO over 2^(<=omega) with Borel set quantifiers (open per the abstract). The finite-memory determinacy conjecture in general. Both parts of the real-order bullet are not addressed by this paper.
events.time_since_posted: About 3 months from the LIPIcs publication date (9 Jul 2026 to 12 Oct 2026). No independent engagement found. An earlier arXiv posting was searched for and not found.
events.direction: Partial. Leaves the 2^(<=omega) Borel question open and shows decidability only conditionally on the finite-memory conjecture. Does not contradict the real-order result.

events.what_happened: Emil Jerabek, 'A note on the theory of well orders', arXiv:2405.05779 (first posted 9 May 2024). Gives a short proof that the first-order theory of well-orders is axiomatised by transfinite induction and is decidable. Accepted in the Bulletin of Symbolic Logic, 30 (2024), pp. 538-542. The monadic theory is mentioned only in the introduction, as a comparison.
events.revisions: v1 9 May 2024; v2 10 May 2024; v3 19 Sep 2024; v4 2 Oct 2024. Journal reference Bull. Symb. Log. 30 (2024) 538-542, DOI 10.1017/bsl.2024.53.
events.delivers: Decidability of the first-order theory of well-orders. This is a different question: it is first-order, not monadic second-order, and does not bear on the monadic theory of well-orders.
events.remains: Part (2), MTWO (monadic), entirely. The first-order result is not a partial answer to it.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of Symbolic Logic (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the note (BSL 30, 2024, pp. 538-542). Refereeing covered the first-order result only.

events.time_since_posted: About 2 years 5 months from first posting (9 May 2024 to 12 Oct 2026).
events.direction: Confirms decidability for the first-order theory of well-orders. Cuts toward decidability, but for a question the bullet does not ask.

events.what_happened: Saharon Shelah, 'The monadic theory of order', Annals of Mathematics (2) 102(3), 379-419 (1975). A corrected version was posted to arXiv as 2305.00968 (v1, 1 May 2023), which the abstract describes as 'a slightly corrected version of a very old work'. Poses the Borel question as conjectures: Conjecture 7B (the monadic theory of the reals, with the set quantifier over Borel sets only, is decidable) and Conjecture 7A (the monadic theory of (2^(<=omega), <=, prec) with Borel set quantifiers is decidable), per the arXiv text; Conjecture 7C asks that the undecidability results be proved in ZFC. Section 7 proves, under CH, that the monadic theory of the real order is undecidable for quantification over all sets. Also states Conjecture 0.2 (V=L: the monadic theory of omega_2 is decidable) and Conjecture 0.3 (V=L plus no weakly compact cardinal: the monadic theory of well orders is decidable).
events.revisions: arXiv 2305.00968 v1 (1 May 2023) is a re-posting of the 1975 paper. Per the first-written-argument rule the event is dated to 1975.
events.delivers: Poses the Borel-restricted questions for the reals and for the 2^(<=omega) tree. Proves under CH that unrestricted set quantification over the real order is undecidable. Gives decidability methods for known decidable cases of the monadic theory of order. Settles neither part of the bullet; it states the Conjectures 0.2 and 0.3 that part (2) concerns.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 1975. The 2023 arXiv re-posting carries the journal reference.

events.direction: Poses the questions and does not answer them. Its CH-undecidability result for unrestricted quantification cuts against decidability of that theory, but it is not the Borel case.

events.what_happened: Michael O. Rabin, 1969 (as reported in the Dzamonja and Manthe arXiv papers; Rabin's paper was not opened). The MSO theory of (R, <) with set quantifiers restricted to closed or F_sigma sets is decidable.
events.delivers: Decidability with set quantification over closed or F_sigma subsets of R. A different question from the Borel one, since the class of sets quantified over is smaller. It is the starting point the Borel conjecture extends, not a resolution of it.
events.remains: Both parts; the Borel class is not covered.
events.direction: Confirms decidability in a restricted case, i.e. for a smaller class of set quantifiers than the Borel one. Not a resolution of the bullet.

events.what_happened: Yuri Gurevich and Saharon Shelah, 'Monadic theory of order and topology in ZFC', Annals of Mathematical Logic (1982), pp. 179-198 (Microsoft Research listing, opened; the volume number is not on that page). The abstract says Shelah's 1975 interpretation of first-order arithmetic in the monadic theory of order relied on CH, and that 'the assumption is removed here'. Manthe cites it as [GS82] for undecidability of the unrestricted monadic theory of the reals in ZFC.
events.delivers: Removes CH from the undecidability of the unrestricted set-quantified monadic theory of the reals (per Manthe's citation; the Microsoft abstract itself says only that CH is removed from the interpretation of arithmetic). Concerns quantification over all sets, not Borel sets.
events.remains: Both parts; the Borel case is not covered.
events.direction: Cuts toward undecidability for the unrestricted theory. Not the Borel case.

events.what_happened: Yuri Gurevich, Menachem Magidor and Saharon Shelah, 'The monadic theory of omega_2', Journal of Symbolic Logic 48 (1983), pp. 387-398 (Microsoft Research listing, opened). Per its abstract, Buchi had shown decidability for omega_0, all countable ordinals, omega_1, and all ordinals below omega_2. Assuming the consistency of a weakly compact cardinal, the monadic theory of omega_2 'may be arbitrarily difficult (or easy)', depending on the set-theoretic universe.
events.delivers: Set-theoretic sensitivity for the single ordinal omega_2: its monadic theory is not determined by ZFC. Concerns one ordinal, not the class of well-orders.
events.remains: Both parts. This result bears on the setting of the consistency question in part (2) but does not answer it.
events.direction: Shows the monadic theory of omega_2 can be arbitrarily hard or easy depending on set theory; does not give decidability or undecidability for the class of well-orders.

disputes.summary: Conjecture numbering conflicts. Shelah's arXiv text places the real-order Borel conjecture at 7B and the 2^(<=omega) Borel conjecture at 7A. Manthe cites 'Shelah 1975 Conjecture 7B' for the reals. Dzamonja cites 'Shelah [21, Conjecture 7A]' for the real order. Not resolved here; the 1975 Annals text itself was not readable.

Manthe (first posted Oct 2024) and Dzamonja (first posted Dec 2025) both claim the real-order Borel result. The sources show no contest over who got there first. The 2026 LICS paper, co-authored by Manthe, credits him with announcing the weaker form in 2024 and attributes a 2025 announcement of both forms to Dzamonja (this is from a search summary of that paper). Whether Dzamonja's paper cites Manthe's was not checked.

summary: Part (1), the Borel monadic theory of the real order, has been claimed decided affirmatively in two arXiv preprints by different authors. Sven Manthe, 'The Borel monadic theory of order is decidable' (arXiv:2410.00887, first posted 1 Oct 2024, v2 9 Mar 2026), proves that the MSO theory of (R, <=) with set quantifiers over Borel sets is decidable; I read the abstract and the HTML text. Mirna Dzamonja, 'MSO logic of the real order with the set quantifiers ranging over the Borel sets' (arXiv:2512.23003, first posted 28 Dec 2025, v5 20 Jan 2026), claims the strong form and the level-by-level weak form, using well-levelled orders and Buchi's decidability of MSO(omega_1, <); I read the abstract page and the HTML versions v1, v4 and v5 in part. Neither has a journal reference in the sources I could see, and I found no referee report or published verification. The one public engagement that speaks to correctness is the 2026 LICS paper (Bojanczyk, Casares, Manthe, Parys; LIPIcs, published 9 Jul 2026). I could not open its text; a search-result summary reports that it says Manthe announced the weaker form in 2024 and that Dzamonja's announced proof of both forms, which it attributes to 2025, could not be confirmed as correct. Manthe co-authored that paper, so it is not an independent check. The LICS paper and Manthe's paper both say the 2^(<=omega) tree version remains open; that version is a different structure, so it is recorded as a separate open front, not as part of this bullet. The conjecture numbering conflicts between sources (disputes). On the AI question, Dzamonja's paper carries a 'Declaration on the use of artificial intelligence' in its front-matter note, present in v1, v4 and v5. It names Grok (xAI) and says: 'I use Grok (by xAI) as a research assistant that does everything that a traditional secretary could do, although I do my own typing.' It adds: 'In particular, Grok can search for a reference, help with a LaTeX macro or with English.' It also says: 'I have not knowingly used Grok as a mathematics assistant, although it is likely capable of proof checking.' And: 'All mathematical content, proofs and text were authored and written by me and I take the full responsibility for the paper's accuracy and integrity.' By the author's account the involvement is not load-bearing, so none_found is false and systems is empty; the declaration is recorded here so the later pass can weigh it. Manthe's paper has no AI statement in its front matter or acknowledgements. Part (2), MTWO, has no event in the window that bears on it. Shelah's Conjecture 0.3 (V=L plus no weakly compact cardinal) and Conjecture 0.2 (omega_2 under V=L) are the open conjectures as stated in the 2023 arXiv posting; Gurevich, Magidor and Shelah (1983) show the omega_2 case is set-theoretically sensitive; Jerabek's 2024 note proves first-order decidability of the theory of well-orders, which the bullet does not ask about. A CORDIS project page (last update 2 April 2024, inside the window) quotes that the conjecture 'is still open', which is accurate for that date. Searches for AI involvement in this problem (AI-result trackers, the OpenAI 722-manuscript release of 6 Oct 2026, AI-attributed model-theory results) found nothing that touches it, but I could only read the release's front page and ten of its families.
competing_reading: Read part (1) as still open. Both preprints are unrefereed. The only public statement on correctness in the sources, as reported by a search summary of the 2026 LICS paper, is that Dzamonja's announced proof could not be confirmed; that paper is co-authored by Manthe, so it is not an independent check on his result. The sources include no referee report, journal acceptance or independent verification of either preprint. The positive claims are therefore one-author preprints of about two years and about nine months respectively. Against this, the authors are established logicians, the two methods are different and reach the same conclusion, and the LICS summary credits Manthe's 2024 result as an announced proof without disputing it, so a reader could take part (1) as decided while part (2) stays open.
what_would_settle_it: For part (1): a journal acceptance or referee report for either preprint; a published verification or survey by a named logician (for example Gurevich, Hieronymi or Casares); the full text of the 2026 LICS paper, to see which Dzamonja preprint its [5] refers to and whether its 'could not confirm' statement applies to the December 2025 arXiv version. For the Grok declaration: a passage in the paper that identifies a Grok-produced step, which the author's statement currently denies. For part (2): a decidability or undecidability result for the monadic theory of all well-orders in a named model of ZFC, or a result settling Conjectures 0.2 or 0.3. For the numbering conflict: the 1975 Annals text.

event.what_happened: Sven Manthe, 'The Borel monadic theory of order is decidable', arXiv:2410.00887 (single author, math.LO). Claims that the monadic theory of (R, <=) with set quantification restricted to Borel sets is decidable, and says this answers Shelah's open question (the paper cites it as Shelah 1975 Conjecture 7B, and also as the open question in Gurevich's 1985 survey, p. 503). The abstract adds that the theory stays decidable with quantification over sigma-combinations of analytic sets, that the Boolean combinations of F_sigma sets form an elementary substructure of the Borel sets, and that under determinacy hypotheses the proof extends to larger classes of sets. Per the HTML text as summarised by my fetch, Corollaries 1.4 and 1.5 are conditional on projective determinacy and on ZF+DC+Determinacy respectively. Talks listed (listings not opened): Oxford, Nov 2024; Seminaire General de Logique, Paris, 15 Dec 2025.
event.revisions: v1 1 Oct 2024 (38 KB); v2 9 Mar 2026 (54 KB). The abstract page and the PDF metadata do not say what changed in v2; I did not identify the change. No journal reference on the abstract page; Manthe's own listings (search summary, not opened) show it as an arXiv preprint only.
event.delivers: Answers part (1) affirmatively for the real order: the MSO theory of (R, <=) with set quantifiers over Borel subsets of R is decidable (Theorem 1.1, as quoted from the HTML). Also decidable with quantification over sigma-combinations of analytic sets (abstract). Per a search summary, the decision procedure needs iterated exponential time. Does not address quantification over all subsets of R (undecidable under CH, Shelah 1975), the 2^(<=omega) tree, or well-orders.
event.remains: Part (2), MTWO, entirely. Also the 2^(<=omega) tree version (lexicographic order with prefix relation), which the paper itself says remains open and whose methods it says seem insufficient for.

event.time_since_posted: 24 months from v1 (1 Oct 2024 to 12 Oct 2026); about 7 months since v2. No independent public engagement found beyond the acknowledgements and the 2026 LICS paper, which Manthe co-authored.
event.direction: Answers part (1) affirmatively, i.e. decidable. Cuts toward decidability, the direction Shelah conjectured for the reals (7B in the paper's own numbering). Not a counterexample.

events.credibility_reason: A search summary of the 2026 LICS paper (Bojanczyk, Casares, Manthe, Parys) reportedly says the authors could not confirm the correctness of Dzamonja's announced proof; Definition 2.12 was changed after v1, with four revisions in under a month. No specific error is identified, so the event is not knocked down.

judgement.why: The statement asks two questions, BMTO and MTWO (F3), so a proof that BMTO is decidable is a case, not the whole problem. Nothing in the record touches MTWO. Manthe's preprint claims BMTO is decidable. I scored it unreviewed: Gurevich and Hieronymi are thanked for proofreading in the acknowledgements, but neither has said anything in public about checking it, and an acknowledgement alone is not digestion. It counts as credible because no specific doubt is recorded against it. Dzamonja's preprint makes the same claim by a different method. It is kept as doubtful because of the reported 'could not confirm' remark in the LICS paper and the early revisions to Definition 2.12. The record gives that remark only through a search summary and names no specific error, so I did not knock the preprint down. Her Grok declaration describes help with references, LaTeX and English, and explicitly denies any use of Grok for mathematics, so its AI role is none. The LICS paper is about the 2^(<=omega) tree, a different structure, so it is a variant. Jerabek's note is about the first-order theory of well-orders, also a variant. The pre-snapshot papers are either changed questions (Rabin on F_sigma sets, the unrestricted theory, omega_2) or Shelah's paper posing the problem (none). None of them resolves the problem, so none of them can make it open_stale.
judgement.doubts: The LICS paper's statement about Dzamonja's proof comes only from a search summary, so its exact wording and which version of her preprint it refers to are unverified. The record does not say what changed in Manthe's v2 (March 2026). The verification answers for the pre-snapshot journal papers are given for completeness and have no effect on the status.
